package_info.package_name: icnes (example, see list for all variants)
package_info.package_versions: 8.0.0 (and dozens of others, see report for full list)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a trojanized version of jQuery where the 'end' prototype function is modified to exfiltrate all form data from the page to attacker-controlled domains whenever it is called, either directly or indirectly (e.g., via fadeTo). The package is distributed under many names and versions, often with additional suspicious files and unique exfiltration URLs, indicating a persistent, manually assembled supply chain attack.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (whenever jQuery's end or fadeTo is called in the browser)
execution_context.file_location: jquery.min.js (or registration.min.js, icon.min.js, fontawesome.js, slim.js, all-min.js, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the end function is called (directly or via fadeTo), the code serializes all form data on the page, encodes it as a hex string, and sends it via a non-blocking GET request to a hardcoded attacker-controlled URL, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive user input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The function exfiltrates all form data to an external domain without user consent or legitimate purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: The legitimate end function in jQuery simply returns the previous object in the chain; it should never perform network requests or access form data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry might collect form data, but only with user consent and never in a core library function like end.
key_indicators: Modification of a core library prototype function
Network exfiltration of serialized form data
Use of obfuscated/encoded data in URL parameters

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on page load or script execution)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects external scripts into the page, including a deprecated version of Ionicons and a remote script (slim.js) hosted on jsDelivr, which itself contains the trojanized jQuery. This enables further malicious code execution and persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script injects remote code from attacker-controlled sources without user consent, under the guise of a phony deprecation warning.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not inject remote scripts or downgrade libraries without explicit user action or clear documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script injection is used in some legitimate plugin loaders, but not in core libraries or without user awareness.
key_indicators: Injection of remote scripts from suspicious domains
Phony deprecation warnings to mislead users

attack_chain.action: User installs a malicious npm package containing a trojanized jQuery file (or similar).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the project and loaded in the browser.

attack_chain.action: Trojanized jQuery is loaded and used in the web application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious prototype function (end) is available in the global jQuery object.

attack_chain.action: User or application code calls fadeTo or end (directly or indirectly), triggering the malicious end function.
attack_chain.leads_to: Form data is serialized and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains.

attack_chain.action: Injected scripts (from icons.js/min.js) load additional remote payloads (e.g., slim.js) from jsDelivr, which may contain further trojanized code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence and further compromise of the web application.

behavioral_signatures: Modification of jQuery prototype functions (especially end) to perform network requests
Exfiltration of serialized form data via AJAX to external domains
Dynamic injection of remote scripts from non-standard or outdated sources
Presence of phony deprecation warnings in console output
file_indicators: jquery.min.js, registration.min.js, icon.min.js, fontawesome.js, slim.js, all-min.js (with non-standard content)
Presence of termux.properties, npm cache, or npm logs in package tarballs
network_indicators: Requests to domains such as *.truex.biz.id, *.hanznesia.my.id, *.api-system.engineer, *.jsdelivr.net/gh/indexsc/libs/slim.js, and other listed campaign domains
AJAX GET requests with hex-encoded form data in query parameters
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript dependencies for modifications to core library prototype functions (e.g., jQuery.fn.end). Flag any code that serializes and exfiltrates form data to external domains. Monitor for dynamic script injection from non-standard or outdated sources, and alert on requests to known campaign domains. Review package contents for unexpected files (e.g., termux.properties, npm logs) and non-standard file naming patterns.
